text.p: Sir Donald Bradman has become the last survivor of the infamous "Bodyline" test series that strained diplomatic relations between Britain and Australia during the early 1930s.
Bradman lost his last remaining team mate when Australian batsman Leo O'Brien died on Thursday, aged 89.
Now aged 88, Bradman is the oldest former Australian test cricketer still alive.
In the 1932-33 Ashes series in Australia, Bradman was targeted by his England opponents who aimed short-pitched leg-side deliveries at his body in an attempt to curb his prolific scoring.
The tactic, dubbed "Bodyline", injured some other batsmen, infuriating Australian crowds. The incidents prompted several terse exchanges between the two governments.
But from England's point of view, the tactic worked. They won the series 4-1 after restricting Bradman to what by his high standards was a moderate average of 56.
There are no surviving England players from the "Bodyline" series.
